**Thinking as this farmer:**

I've been farming this land my whole life. My family has about 10 mu here in Quzhou. The soil is decent — silty loam, good for wheat. My father grew wheat and corn, I grow wheat and corn. There's no reason to change. Cotton prices have been bad, vegetables need too much labor and I can't compete with those big growers. Wheat and corn, that's what the market buys from people like me, and the government still gives some support for grain.

Winter wheat goes in mid-October after I prepare the field — I'll do rotary tillage to break up the soil after last year's corn stubble. I'll use Shimai 15 seed, the extension station has been recommending it for a few years and my neighbor's yield was good. For the corn in summer, I'll buy Xianyu 335 hybrid seed from the county supply shop — I always do, it performs reliably.

Fertilizer: I put down a base of diammonium phosphate and potassium chloride before planting wheat, then add urea at jointing. For corn I do a base application and top-dress at the big bell stage. I probably use a bit more nitrogen than I should — my father always said "feed the crop" — but I'm not going to risk yield.

Irrigation: I pump from the well. Wheat needs water at sowing if the soil is dry, then at jointing and heading — that's three times minimum. Corn usually gets two, sometimes three if July is dry.

Pesticides: wheat gets a herbicide spray in spring and a fungicide if I see flag leaf disease. Corn usually just one herbicide pass.
